steps.title: JavaScript ES6+ Essentials
steps.description: Master modern JavaScript features like arrow functions, destructuring, spread operators, and modules required for React development.

lesson.title: JavaScript ES6+ Essentials for React
lesson.introduction: Before diving into React, you must master specific modern JavaScript features. React relies heavily on these ES6+ patterns to manage data, pass information between components, and keep code concise. Mastering these will make reading React code feel natural rather than overwhelming.

sections.title: Arrow Functions
sections.content: Arrow functions provide a shorter syntax for writing functions. In React, they are used everywhere: defining components, handling clicks, and mapping through lists. A key feature is the 'implicit return,' where if the function is a single line, you can omit the curly braces and the 'return' keyword.

sections.title: Destructuring
sections.content: Destructuring is a way to 'unpack' values from arrays or properties from objects into distinct variables. In React, this is the primary way we extract data from 'props' (the data passed to a component) and 'state' (the data held within a component). Instead of writing 'props.name' repeatedly, you can simply destructure 'name' from the props object.

sections.title: Spread and Rest Operators
sections.content: The spread operator (...), also known as the 'triple dot,' allows you to quickly copy all elements from an array or all properties from an object into a new one. In React, we never modify data directly (a concept called 'immutability'). Instead, we use the spread operator to create a copy of our existing data, add or change something, and then save that new copy.

sections.title: ES Modules (Import and Export)
sections.content: Modules allow you to break your code into separate files. This is how React applications are built: every component is usually its own file. You use 'export' to make a function or component available to the rest of your app, and 'import' to bring those components into the files where you want to use them.

keyTakeaways: Arrow functions offer a concise syntax and are used for almost all functional logic in React.
Destructuring is the standard way to extract data from objects and arrays.
The spread operator (...) is essential for updating state without mutating the original data.
Modules (import/export) are the foundation of the component-based architecture in React.

steps.title: JSX and Component Fundamentals
steps.description: Understand JSX syntax and learn how to build reusable UI elements using functional components.

lesson.title: Mastering JSX and Functional Components
lesson.introduction: Welcome to the foundation of React development. In this lesson, you will learn how to write UI using JSX and how to structure your application into reusable functional components.

sections.title: What is JSX?
sections.content: JSX stands for JavaScript XML, a syntax extension that allows you to write HTML-like code directly within your JavaScript files. It provides a visual representation of the UI, making your code easier to read and maintain while being transformed into standard JavaScript objects under the hood.

sections.title: Embedding Expressions in JSX
sections.content: To make your UI dynamic, you can embed any valid JavaScript expression directly inside your JSX using curly braces. This allows you to display variables, perform mathematical operations, or call functions within your markup.

sections.title: Component Composition
sections.content: React encourages a pattern called composition, where you build complex interfaces by nesting smaller, specialized components inside larger ones. This modular approach makes your code more readable and easier to maintain.

examples.title: Using Expressions in JSX

keyTakeaways: JSX allows you to write HTML-like structures directly inside JavaScript.
Use curly braces `{}` to inject dynamic JavaScript values into your JSX.
Build complex UIs by nesting small, reusable components within larger ones.

lesson.title: Mastering Control Flow in JavaScript
lesson.introduction: Control flow refers to the order in which the computer executes the statements in your script. By mastering conditional statements and loops, you can transform static code into dynamic programs that react to different inputs.

sections.title: Conditional Statements: Making Decisions
sections.content: Conditional statements allow your code to branch into different paths based on whether a condition is true or false. Using 'if', 'else if', and 'else', you can execute specific blocks of code only when certain criteria are met.
